keyVerseText: And David arose, and went with all the people that were with him from Baale of Judah, to bring up from thence the ark of God, whose name is called by the name of the LORD of hosts that dwelleth between the cherubims. Baale: or, Baalah, that is, Kirjathjearim whose name: or, at which the name, even the name of the LORD of hosts, was called upon
rootMeaning: The term "בַּעֲלֵי יְהוּדָה" (Baʻălêy Yᵉhûwdâh) stems from the plural form of the root word בַּעַל (baʻal), which carries a range of meanings including lord, master, husband, or chief man. Combined with יְהוּדָה (Judah), it literally means "masters of Judah" or "lords of Judah." This etymology highlights a sense of authority and ownership, emphasizing those who hold power or stewardship within the territory or people of Judah, beyond just a simple place name or title.
usageInScripture: This phrase occurs only once in Scripture, specifically in 2 Samuel 6:2, where it is translated as "that were with him from Baale of Judah." The term refers both to a location—also known as Kirjath-jearim—and implicitly to the people associated with that place. The translation as "Baale of Judah" or "Baale-Judah" reflects the dual understanding of the term as both a geographical site and a designation of those who belong to or are under the authority of Judah, indicating a close link between place and people in the biblical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding "בַּעֲלֵי יְהוּדָה" as "masters of Judah" or a place named for such lords deepens our appreciation of God's providence in history, where human authority and divine sovereignty intersect. The term reminds believers that earthly leaders and communities are under God's ultimate lordship, especially as the ark of God is brought from this place. It also points to the faithfulness required of those who hold stewardship within God's people, foreshadowing Christ as the true Lord over Judah and all creation. This word thus encourages reflection on the relationship between human authority, place, and God's covenantal presence.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Samuel 6:2, the phrase "Baale of Judah" identifies the origin of the people accompanying David as they bring up the ark of God. This designation situates the event within a specific geographical and cultural context, emphasizing the unity and support of Judah's leaders or inhabitants in this pivotal moment. The term enriches the verse by linking the physical journey of the ark with the spiritual leadership and community of Judah, highlighting the convergence of God's presence with His chosen people.
